prompt:
Create an original slow, dreamy, intimate dream-pop ballad, about two and a half minutes long, at about 70 BPM, in A major. A clean electric guitar drenched in long reverb plays slow, arpeggiated major-seventh chords; a warm, round bass; very soft brushed drums that enter only at the first chorus and stay quiet; a faint organ pad underneath. A hushed, breathy, gentle androgynous lead vocal, sung close to the microphone, unhurried, tender and melancholic, romantic and spacious, like a grey afternoon that slowly turns warm. Long instrumental intro of about 15 seconds before the voice. Sparse arrangement with lots of air; no loud climax, no belting, no harmonies stacked high, no electronic beats. Sing these original lyrics exactly:

[Intro]
(slow reverb guitar, no voice)

[Verse 1]
Grey on the window, rain on the street
Everyone passing, nobody sees
You held the paper, warm in your hand
I didn't ask you, you understand

[Chorus]
Slow down, slow down
Stay at my side
Tell me your name
And I'll tell you mine

[Verse 2]
Boots on the pavement, laces undone
Half of a drawing I never got done
You waited still like you had all day
I nearly told you to go away

[Chorus]
Slow down, slow down
Stay at my side
Tell me your name
And I'll tell you mine

[Bridge]
Round the corner
Don't let go

[Outro]
Slow down
Slow down
(guitar rings out)
